_comment: Known mobile viewport offenders (#2813). Each entry allows specific finding
kinds on one surface: 'overflow', 'tap-target', 'wide-table', and on native
list surfaces 'row-height' and 'first-row-low'. Anything not listed here
fails the spec.
'row-height' (#4200): a data row of a list taller than 120px.
'first-row-low' (#4200): the first data row starts more than 400px down the
page. Both are measured only where the list has rows in CI's wp-env data.
Seeded from the first CI run that actually reached the dashboard (#4195) -
before that every surface skipped and the gate measured nothing. The spec
prints the current offenders in this file's exact shape at the end of every
run; paste that in to recalibrate after a wave of fixes. Do not transcribe
from a seeded local install: CI's wp-env data is what the gate measures.
The 71 entries caused by the 34px header home link were removed when #4204
widened it to 48px. The entries left here each have their own offender.
Reseeded for #4232. Every check now runs after a list's rows have loaded
over REST, and a tap target is an element a person can see: content hidden
by an ancestor (the items of a closed menu) and boxes of 1px or less
(visually hidden inputs) are not measured. That removed five entries and
added two that the wait exposed: 'goals' and 'people', for the links inside
their list rows, which had not arrived when the old gate measured.
Reseeded for #4237. An element with pointer-events: none is not a tap
target: in a row-link list the row takes the tap and a link on its title
line (#4224) or a cell marked mobile_plain (#4235) is text on a phone. That
removed 'people' and 'players' and added nothing. 'goals' stays: the goal
title on the subtitle line of each row is still a live link, 18px high.
'goals' removed for #4241: the goal title column is mobile_plain, and the
gate reported the entry as no longer offending.
'teams: row-height' is accepted by design, not a to-do. The teams list
shows cards, not table rows, and a team card of about 171px is the intended
size (owner decision, 2026-10-04). Keep the entry; do not shrink the cards
to clear it.
The job is non-blocking (continue-on-error in e2e.yml) until every entry
but the accepted one is gone; then drop continue-on-error.
Removing an entry is the goal. The spec reports any entry that no longer
offends, because a stale allowance is where the next real regression hides.
